question:
(a) Explain why a prism can produce a spectrum from white light.
(b) Why does a rectangular glass slab not produce a spectrum with angular separation like a prism, although refraction occurs in it?
(c) Mention the main role of wavelength in dispersion.

options.A:
(a) A prism produces a spectrum because all colours have the same refractive index and deviate equally.
(b) A glass slab gives more angular separation because its faces are parallel.
(c) Wavelength has no role in dispersion.
options.B:
(a) A prism splits white light due to reflection at its two faces.
(b) A glass slab fails to form a spectrum because no refraction occurs in it.
(c) The main role of wavelength is to change brightness only.
options.C:
(a) White light has colours of different wavelengths, and a prism's refractive index depends on wavelength, so colours deviate by different angles and form a spectrum; red deviates least and violet most.
(b) In a rectangular glass slab the faces are parallel, so refraction at the second face makes emergent rays of each colour parallel to the incident ray; there is no angular separation as in a prism with inclined faces.
(c) Wavelength dependence of refractive index is the main cause of dispersion: shorter wavelengths generally have higher refractive index and deviate more.
options.D:
(a) A prism forms a spectrum because it absorbs different colours.
(b) A slab produces no spectrum because it is opaque.
(c) Longer wavelengths always have higher refractive index and deviate more.
